name: Ambient-Cube Corner-Descent Criterion
statement: Let $A\subsetneq Q_E$ be nonempty and ample. A sequence of corner deletions takes the ambient cube $Q_E$ to $A$ if and only if the cube complement $Q_E\setminus A$ is dismantlable ample.
proof: Write $B=Q_E\setminus A$, which is ample by complement duality. If $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ are deleted from the cube, every residual complement $\{b_1,\ldots,b_j\}$ is ample. Reversing these ample prefixes gives a corner peeling of $B$. Conversely, reverse a peeling of $B$. Its successive prefixes $B_j$ are ample, so their complements are ample; the ample corner-deletion criterion makes each next $b_j$ a corner of $Q_E\setminus B_{j-1}$, producing the descent to $A$.
comments: This converts generation by deletion from a cube into an ordinary peelability test for the complement.
